translations.translatedText: # Sunday 22.11.2020 (radio)
Viking Grace. Unemployment. Christmas Street. Weather forecast.
## Viking Grace got off the rocks
![The Viking Line passenger ship Viking Grace, which ran aground, in the port of Mariehamn on 22 November 2020.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11660448)
Open image viewer
The Viking Grace in the port of Mariehamn on Sunday. Photo: Niclas Nordlund / Lehtikuva
The Viking Grace ship has been able to continue its journey from Åland. The Viking Grace was first freed from the rocks and towed to the port of Mariehamn.

Divers checked the bottom of the ship. The bottom was intact, and the authorities gave the ship permission to sail to Turku on its own engines. The passengers of the ship also got to Turku on the ship.
The Viking Grace ran aground on Saturday near the port of Mariehamn. Nobody was hurt.
The Viking Grace will go from Turku to a shipyard for repairs. Another ship will take the place of the Viking Grace on the Turku–Mariehamn–Stockholm route in the meantime.
## Unemployment is lasting longer for many
![A form for earnings-related unemployment allowance being filled in.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11452127)
Open image viewer
An unemployed person is filling in a form to apply for earnings-related allowance. Photo: Tiina Jutila / Yle

The coronavirus crisis is lengthening unemployment for many Finns. The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment estimates that the number of long-term unemployed will grow a lot in the coming years.
A long-term unemployed person is someone who has been unemployed for 12 months or longer.

Before the coronavirus time, there were over 60,000 long-term unemployed people in Finland. Now it is estimated that the number of long-term unemployed may rise to over 113,000 during next year and the year after.
## The Christmas season was opened
![Helsinki's Christmas opening in 2020 was celebrated on Senate Square on a sunny Sunday.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11660519)
Open image viewer
There was a programme for children at Helsinki's Christmas opening. Photo: Katriina Laine / Yle

The Christmas season has been opened in Finland again, in Helsinki. On Sunday afternoon the Christmas lights were lit on Aleksanterinkatu, and there was a programme for children on Senate Square. There was also a Father Christmas on Senate Square. The event was also shown on the internet.
The opening of Christmas Street in Helsinki was done in a slightly different way this year than before. Because of the coronavirus situation, there was no traditional parade.
The Christmas lights on Christmas Street in Helsinki can be seen until the end of January. The opening of Christmas Street is a traditional event in Helsinki. It started in 1949.
## Weather
![Snow and sleet on a car window.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-7963028)
Open image viewer
It may snow in northern Finland. Photo: Sakari Partanen / Yle
The weather changes to rainier in the coming week.

On Monday the sky is cloudy at times, and especially in the middle of the country there will be rain and sleet. In the north it will snow or rain. On Monday the daytime temperature varies between 0 and +5, and in Lapland between 0 and -5 degrees.
On Tuesday the weather is drier.
